author: reek
body: Runtime coverage for the animation half of the engine foreword. These chapters could not type-check until CL 7517 and have never run; the migration to Real was checked by the compiler, and the compiler cannot see a scale factor.

author: reek
body: The invariants here are the ones a wrong conversion breaks and a type does not catch. Identity means identity: skinning a vertex through an identity bone leaves the vertex exactly where it was, and any factor lost or gained at the Vertex-to-Vec3 boundary moves it. A blend at nought is the first pose and a blend at one is the second, exactly, or the thousandths were misread. Weights that sum to one preserve position however they are split between bones.

author: reek
body: Writing these found a bug the type checker had passed: bp-identity scaled by a thousand, because Vec3 was fixed-point when Skinning was written and a thousand meant unity there, while mat4-scale takes 1.0 as identity. The identity pose was a thousandfold magnification. Scene3D's t3-identity had the same defect.

author: reek
body: A bone that translates by a known amount, so a skinned vertex has an answer that can be written down rather than merely eyeballed.
